ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

gustilo — pattern 3

A high-energy motorcycle crash causes a comminuted open tibial fracture. After debridement there is extensive soft-tissue injury, but viable local tissues adequately cover the bone without a flap. Perfusion is intact and no arterial repair is required. Which Gustilo–Anderson grade best describes the injury?

  1. Type II
  2. Type IIIA
  3. Type IIIB
  4. Type IIIC
  5. Type I
Answer and explanation

Type IIIA

Type IIIA: A severe open fracture with adequate viable soft-tissue coverage of the bone.

Option explanations

Type IIIA: Type IIIA: A severe open fracture with adequate viable soft-tissue coverage of the bone.

Type IIIB: Type IIIB describes an open fracture with extensive soft-tissue loss, periosteal stripping and inadequate bone coverage requiring flap reconstruction. The case instead matches Type IIIA.

Type IIIC: Type IIIC describes an open fracture associated with an arterial injury requiring repair, regardless of wound size. The case instead matches Type IIIA.

Type I: Type I describes a low-energy open fracture with a clean wound under 1 cm and minimal soft-tissue damage. The case instead matches Type IIIA.

Type II: Type II describes an open fracture with a wound over 1 cm but without extensive soft-tissue destruction, flaps or avulsion. The case instead matches Type IIIA.
